summary: The paper presents two Grover-based simulator demonstrations for portfolio selection: QES-based conditional slicing over 8 efficient portfolios using 18 qubits, and GAS-based maximum Sharpe-ratio selection over the same 8 portfolios using 37 qubits. Both experiments were implemented with IBM Qiskit simulators and rely on classical mean-variance preprocessing; the paper reports successful small-scale execution but no empirical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Grover-based conditional slicing to select portfolios whose returns exceed a threshold and standard deviations fall below a threshold, implemented with QES and explicit oracles on Qiskit simulators.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Exponential Search (QES) with explicit comparison oracles for portfolio selection

hyperparameters.thresholding: returns > S1 and standard deviations < S2

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Threshold values supplied from classical efficient-frontier portfolios; QES starts with m=1 and random j in [0,m).

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Eight portfolio return values and eight standard deviation values are encoded; indices use 3 qubits for N=8. Values are phase-encoded and compared via a GT-gate after phase estimation. The oracle marks portfolios satisfying the threshold conditions.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Select portfolios with returns above a desired threshold and standard deviations below a desired threshold from a classical efficient frontier.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Conditional filtering via Grover oracle; no penalty terms. Comparison implemented with GT-gates and uncomputation.

problem_instance.description: Selection among efficient portfolios using return and risk thresholds.

dataset_specification.description: Subsample of efficient portfolios; eight values for returns and eight values for standard deviations.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Efficient portfolios generated classically by mean-variance optimization with no-short-selling; values restricted to [0,1); integer parts not compared in the reported experiment.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Implemented on simulators; successful retrieval of desired portfolios reported for the small-scale example.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical mean-variance optimization (no-short-selling) to generate efficient portfolios
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical mean-variance optimization to obtain efficient frontier; subsampling to eight values; risk-free rate not used in this experiment.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement outcome interpreted as selected portfolio index/value.

speedup_claims.conditions: QES on a list of size N with M solutions; expected O(sqrt(N/M)) oracle calls
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports simulator implementation and asymptotic complexity, but no wall-clock benchmark against a classical implementation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N/M)) calls to the oracle for QES; O(sqrt(N)) for quantum counting and GAS subroutines
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N) for unstructured search; classical mean-variance optimization not characterized in the paper

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: At least 18 qubits for the reported small instance; practical advantage would require much larger problem sizes and hardware execution beyond simulators.
limiting_factors: Classical preprocessing required to generate efficient frontier
No runtime comparison against a strong classical baseline

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the circuits were implemented using IBM Qiskit simulators and no physical QPU is named.
18 qubits reported in the paper for Circuit 2: 15 qubits for GT-gate plus 3 qubits for indexing eight values.
Circuit depth and gate counts are not reported explicitly.
The paper reports successful simulator implementation of QES-based portfolio selection, but no experimental quantum advantage over classical methods.

experiments.description: Grover Adaptive Search (GAS) used to find the portfolio with the maximum Sharpe ratio from the same eight efficient portfolios, implemented on Qiskit simulators.

algorithm.variant: Grover Adaptive Search (GAS) for maximum Sharpe ratio selection
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial threshold chosen as a uniformly random portfolio index; later thresholds updated from QES outcomes.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Sharpe ratios for eight portfolios are encoded; 3 qubits for indices and 15 qubits for GT-gate comparison of phase-encoded values. GAS iteratively marks items below the current threshold and searches for a better one.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find the portfolio with the maximum Sharpe ratio.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Iterative Grover-based thresholding via GAS; no penalty terms.

problem_instance.description: Maximum Sharpe ratio selection among efficient portfolios.

dataset_specification.description: Eight portfolio Sharpe ratios derived from the efficient portfolios; risk-free rate set to 0%.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Sharpe ratios computed classically from portfolio returns and standard deviations; all values in [0,1); integer parts not compared.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Index of the highest-Sharpe-ratio portfolio successfully obtained in simulation.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical computation of Sharpe ratios and classical mean-variance optimization to generate the candidate portfolios
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of Sharpe ratios with risk-free rate 0%; efficient frontier generated classically; subsampling to eight values.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement outcome interpreted as the index of the maximum-Sharpe-ratio portfolio.

speedup_claims.conditions: GAS on a list of size N; expected O(sqrt(N)) oracle calls
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical runtime comparison is reported; the paper only states asymptotic complexity and successful simulation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N)) calls to the oracle for GAS
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N) for unstructured search; classical Sharpe-ratio maximization over the candidate list not characterized in the paper

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: At least 37 qubits for the reported small instance; practical advantage would require larger instances and hardware execution.
limiting_factors: Classical Sharpe-ratio computation and mean-variance preprocessing are required
No empirical comparison showing quantum outperforming classical search

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the circuits were implemented using IBM Qiskit simulators and no physical QPU is named.
37 qubits reported in the paper for Circuit 3: 15 qubits for GT-gate, 3 qubits for indices, and additional registers for the two-list oracle.
Circuit depth and gate counts are not reported explicitly.
The paper reports successful simulator implementation of GAS for maximum Sharpe-ratio selection, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.
